Mr.Jahangir M. Poonegar, learned counsel for the appe  Ms.Priti Keshwani, learned counsel for respondent No.
 ORDER

The appellant has filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 16.03.2022 passed by the VI Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.2312/2021 challenging the quantum of compensation on the ground of income assessed by the Tribunal.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The factum of the accident and the liability of the Insurance Company are not in dispute.

3. The brief facts giving rise to the case are that on 28.05.2021 at around 5:30 PM near Love-kush Square, Sanwer Road, Indore, the appellant was going with Mariamma Yohanan, who was working as an Executive at Schon Pharmaceuticals Company Ltd., Indore.
The scooter bearing registration number MP-09-SU-0384 was being driven by Mariamma, while the appellant was pillion rider.
Both were returning to their respective homes NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17234 2 MA-2183-2022 after completing their duty hours at the said company.

3.1 When they reached near Love-kush Square, a vehicle (Bharat-Benz Trolla) bearing registration number MP-09-HH-9262 driven by respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner came from behind and hit the scooter.
As a result, the appellant fell down and the said vehicle crushed her right leg and dragged her about 20 ft., due to which her right leg got dismembered at the spot from right thigh.
She also sustained several grievous injuries on various parts of her body.
The appellant was immediately admitted to Aurobindo Hospital, Indore, where she underwent surgery and remained under treatment by various private doctors.
4. The appellant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by her in the aforesaid accident.

sentences.text: Accordingly, awarded compensation of Rs.13,70,880/- after applying the multiplier of 17 and adding 40% towards future prospects.
4.1. In addition, an amount of Rs.33,265/- was awarded towards medical bills, Rs.20,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.10,000/- for special diet and Rs.5,000/- each towards attendant and conveyance.
A further amount of Rs.10,000/- was awarded under the head of future prospects.
In total, the Claims Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.14,54,145/-.
5. Counsel for the appellant submits that the assessment of income by the Claims Tribunal at Rs.8,000/- per month is not correct and proper.

By referring to the findings recorded in paras 33 and 34 of the award, he submits NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17234 3 MA-2183-2022 that the Tribunal has incorrectly disbelieved the income proof produced by the appellant.
It is stated by the appellant that she was working as a Quality Control Chemist.

In support of this assertion, she examined Bhushan Geete (AW-3), who was Senior Chemist in Schon Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Indore and deposed before the Tribunal that the appellant was working as a Quality Control Chemist in the said Company.
5.1. The appellant also exhibited her pay slips for the months of March, April and May as Exs. P-10 to P-12, which demonstrated that she was receiving a salary of Rs.11,500/- per month.
However, the Claims Tribunal did not accept this evidence on the ground that the appellant had not produced her bank passbook or other corroborative documentary evidence.
After discarding the appellant's documentary evidence, her income was assessed on a notional basis at Rs.8,000/- per month treating her as a skilled labourer.
5.2. Learned counsel further submits that the appellant was employed as a Quality Control Chemist in a reputed Pharmaceuticals Company, therefore, the notional income assessed is unreasonably low.
He further submits that even under other heads, the Tribunal has awarded only minimum amounts.

In particular, only Rs.5,000/- each has been awarded for attendant and conveyance,
despite the fact that the appellant has suffered amputation of her right leg.
Thus, the compensation awarded under these heads is grossly inadequate.

6. On the other land, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the findings of the award and submitted that the appellant had NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17234 4 MA-2183-2022 exhibited only three pay slips, whereas she could have easily produced her bank passbook or bank statements to establish that she was receiving a salary of Rs.11,500/- per month.
Thus, she withheld the best available evidence.
Accordingly, the assessment of income of the appellant on notional basis is justified, thus ultimate compensation based on the such assessment does not warrant any interference.
6.1. She also submits that even under the other heads, just and proper compensation has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal and therefore, no interference is warranted.

7. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
Ku.

Kirti Sharma vs Ashok Kumar on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140769317/
2
8. Even from the narration of facts in the FIR, it is evident that the appellant was employed with Schon Pharmaceuticals Ltd. at the time of accident.
This fact cannot be denied in view of the clear and clinching evidence produced by her before the Claims Tribunal.

Witness Bhushan Geete (AW-3)
clearly deposed that the appellant was working as a Quality Control Chemist in the said Company.
He also stated that H.R. Manager Ms. Kirti Sharma had deputed him to appear before the Claims Tribunal in the present case.
8.1. There was no occasion for the Claims Tribunal to disbelieve this fact.
Thus, it appears that the Tribunal has erred in not accepting the statement of the appellant regarding her income, especially in the absence of any contrary material.
It was not the case of the Insurance Company that the salary slips exhibited as Exs. P-10 to P-13 were not genuine.

Therefore, in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17234 5 MA-2183-2022 the considered view of this Court, the income of the appellant ought to be taken at Rs.11,000/- per month.
9. As regards the compensation under other heads, it is observed that except for the amounts awarded towards attendant and conveyance, proper compensation has been awarded.
The compensation under those two heads is accordingly modified to Rs.10,000/- each.
10. In view of the above modifications, the total compensation payable comes to Rs.19,78,225/-.
Since the Claims Tribunal had awarded Rs.14,54,145/-, the appellant is now entitled to an amount of Rs.5,24,080/- over and above the compensation already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application before the Tribunal.
11. The appellant has valued the appeal at Rs.1,00,000/-.
Accordingly, he is directed to pay the deficit court fee within a month from today.
12. In the above terms, the present appeal stands disposed off.
No order as to costs.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Anushree Ku. Kirti Sharma vs Ashok Kumar on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140769317/
